name: Senture (Partner) (2nd Position)
desc:
Federal Employee Insurance Customer Service Agent | $20.18/hr total | Inbound and Some Outbound Survey Calls, No Sales Expected
Company: Senture (TP Gov Services)
Industry: Customer Service

What Your Day Will Look Like:
You work from home and help people with questions about their federal employee insurance benefits and enrollment options. You take inbound calls and make some outbound survey calls. You use web-based systems with dual monitors and several tabs to find answers, verify caller information, and fix or update it. You document each call in a database, follow up with callers when needed, and stick to your weekly schedule. This role is temporary and expected to continue through December. TP Gov Services has an employee transfer program to help people move into other roles when the assignment ends, if they are in good standing and meet the qualifications.

Soft Skills
- Patience and professional courtesy
- Active listening
- Multitasking
- Clear verbal and written communication
- Reliability and schedule adherence
assessment: Yes, expect an assessment. The posting lists pre-employment criteria testing and an internet speed test.
wage: $15.25/hr plus $4.93/hr health and welfare stipend ($20.18/hr total)
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements

Education Minimum: High school diploma or GED
Required Experience: None listed. Prior call center or customer service experience is highly desired.
Preferred Experience: Call center or customer service experience

Required Skills:
- Clear verbal and written communication
- Multitasking
- Strong computer skills, including dual monitors, multiple tabs, and finding information in databases
- Able to sit for long periods
- Webcam use during training and production
- Pass a background investigation and drug screen
- Pass pre-employment criteria testing and an internet speed test
- Enclosed, secure, distraction-free work area
- Non-cellular high speed internet (fiber, DSL, or cable). Hotspots, satellite, and wireless are not allowed.

This role is ideal for someone who:
- Wants a paid, one-week training and a quick start
- Has customer service or call center experience
- Is comfortable learning new systems and finding answers fast
- Can work a schedule that changes week to week

Not a Good Fit for someone who:
- Needs a permanent job (this one is temporary through December)
- Needs guaranteed 40 hour weeks (hours can be as low as 24)
- Has a felony or cannot pass a background investigation
- Cannot use fiber, DSL, or cable internet at home
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
1. Submit application
2. Expect an assessment email
3. Watch for an email inviting you to a prescreening
4. Depending on how well the prescreening goes, expect an email to schedule an interview
This is an estimated process.

Top 10 Resume Keywords
- Customer service
- Call center
- Inbound and outbound calls
- Insurance benefits
- Data entry
- Database documentation
- Multitasking
- Active listening
- Dual monitors
- Schedule adherence

4-5 Interview Questions for this Role:
- Why are you interested in a temporary customer service role helping federal employees with insurance?
- How do you stay organized when you use several screens and tabs at once?
- How do you handle a caller who is upset or confused about their benefits?
- Tell us about a time you gave great customer service. What was the situation, what did you do, and what was the result?
- Tell us about a time you had to learn a new system quickly. What happened, how did you learn it, and how did it turn out?
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
-Pay: $15.25/hr plus a $4.93/hr health and welfare stipend ($20.18/hr total)
-Shift: Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM Central. Schedules are posted weekly and can vary. Minimum schedules may be as low as 24 hours a week, with extra hours during busy periods.
-Benefits: The posting lists a health and welfare stipend. Basic benefits: insurance options, PTO, possible 401k
-Equipment Provided: Yes
-Felony Friendly?: No
-Drug Test: Required. The posting also requires a background investigation.
-Notes: This role is temporary and expected to continue through December. TP Gov Services has an employee transfer program for people in good standing when the assignment ends. Paid training lasts about one week and attendance is required (missing time means removal from the program). Webcam is required during training and production. Applicants must pass an internet speed test and have non-cellular home internet (fiber, DSL, or cable). Hotspots, satellite, and wireless are not allowed. Co-working is not allowed. Military veterans and military spouses are encouraged to apply.
-Career Pathway: Reasonable inferred path: Customer Service Agent → Senior Agent → Team Lead → Quality or Training Specialist → Operations Supervisor. This role builds call handling, benefits knowledge, database documentation, and schedule management skills.
training: About one week of paid training. Attendance at all sessions is required.
